sections.text: How should they do otherwise? O Thou Supremest Self, greater than the Powers of creation, the First Cause, Infinite, the Lord of Lords, the Home of the universe, Imperishable, Being and Not-Being, yet transcending both.
Thou art the Primal God, the Ancient, the Supreme Abode of this universe, the Knower, the Knowledge and the Final Home. Thou fillest everything. Thy form is infinite.

Thou art the Wind, Thou art Death, Thou art the Fire, the Water, the Moon, the Father and the Grandfather. Honour and glory to Thee a thousand and a thousand times! Again and again, salutation be to Thee, O my Lord!

We had been discussing Chapter 11, Viswarupadarshan yoga of the Cosmic form of the Lord. We have seen so far that Arjuna learned from Bhagavan first the nature of the limited self. What is the nature of this conditioned self? He learned that the self is immortal. The conditionings are perishable. The conditionings -- this body, this mind, this intellect -- are perishable.
But the self is imperishable. And therefore, while working in this world, keep that self in mind, identify with that self. But that is not very naturally happening to people. So Bhagavan talked about how to act in this world, addressed Arjuna, that you should act in this world in the spirit of Yajna. You will be then gradually detach yourself from this ego and will be able to identify with yourself. So then obviously Arjuna wanted to know the nature of that imperishable self.
So from chapter seven, Bhagavan said, I am the source of all the beings and things. Aham krutnasya jagadah prabhavaha pralayah t -- I am the source and dissolution of all things and beings in this world. So thats my relationship to you: I am the source of all the beings, and therefore also the source of you. And then he says, matthaha parataram na asti kincit anyat asti dhananjaya -- there is nothing higher than me.
There is nothing higher than this self. Therefore you should identify with the self. But Arjuna obviously was not ready to take this on its face value. The Bhagavan said, I am the source of all the beings and all the things. He wanted to know more. So he said, I want to know in detail your glories.
Because he is still identifying with Krishna as Krishna, and himself as Arjuna. How can Krishna be the Lord of all the beings? Arjuna, identifying with his limited self, is speaking from his egos perspective and projecting his world. Krishna is speaking from his identification with the Supreme. He said, I am the source of all the beings. So Arjuna said, explain to me in detail, because I actually love hearing about your great glories, all the powers of this omnipresent, omniscient being.
So in chapter 10 we have a detailed description of Bhagavan saying that you can see my glory in everything that is splendid, wonderful, strong -- anything where you can find something which catches your eye.
Thats me at the core of all beings. I am the sweetness in sugar, I am the light in sun, I am the liquidity in water. And even he says Dyutam, Chalaya, Tamasmi, even I am the gambling and the fraudulence. Even that also somebody can only cheat you if he is alive and conscious and consciousness is working through him. Everything that you see in this world, the core of all beings and things, is me and me alone. Nothing other than me exists.
Arjuna heard all that, but hes still not satisfied. Hes still not grasping the whole idea of the omniscience and omnipotence of the Lord -- how the Lord can be everywhere. So he says, I want to see it. I have no doubt; you said this and also many others have said so before you. So I have no doubt about it. I take it for granted that what you are saying is correct.
Because time and again, sages after sages from generations have come and confirmed that this is the truth. So I am not doubting it now. You, Krishna, telling me so, I have no doubt -- but I want to see it. And therefore in chapter 11 we see that Krishna grants him this great vision of totality, where Arjuna can see all at once -- the past, present and future, an entire universe in one glimpse. And what he sees is that up till now the things which he has been seeing as different entities are all merged into one.
Theyre all part of the one entity. Therefore he describes and says, Im seeing that you have thousands of mouths and thousands of hands and thousands of legs and thousands of stomachs. Because every stomach is yours, every hand is yours, every mouth is yours. So I see now all of them as part of the one entity. Im seeing wonderful sights -- all these forms and colors and all the deities, things which I have not seen before, I have not even imagined before. Im seeing all of them.
So hes enchanted by that form. But then he sees the other side of it. Other side of creation is always destruction. This is the other side of it. He sees that now all those beings which I see existing in him also rushing towards his mouth to get destroyed. Every name and form in this world is helplessly rushing toward its own destruction within the self which is supporting it.
So he starts getting really nervous about it that everyone is rushing towards your mouth to get destroyed. And I see the great people, the great heroes are helplessly rushing towards your mouth and getting destroyed. And that vision really terrified him. We had this notion about Bhagavan as one who is compassionate, serene, and creative. But the destructive aspect -- we never focus on that. Arjuna, while listening to all the discourses before, all the glories, all the splendid descriptions given --
I am the light in the sun. I am the fragrance in flower. So he was expecting it will be all well and good. Once I see the totality, it will be wonderful. My mind will be at peace. And after that there will be no problem.
But he sees the other side of it. He says everything is getting destroyed. Every name and form is getting destroyed in the being of that great Mahatma, the great person, the Purusha, the one entity. So he says, Im terrified. I cant find my place in life. I dont know where I am and Im losing my bearing.
So tell me, who are you and what are you up to? Because I have never imagined your form like this. See, only in our culture, in our religion, we have terrible forms of God also -- Kali and Shiva doing Tandava and Rudra and Pralaya. But in most cases we want to see him as a very calm, serene, and peaceful God. But when you want to understand God in totality, Bhagavan says, you have to know this also.
So he sees this destruction happening. Bhagavan says, I am the world-devouring time. Kalosmi -- I am that time which devours everything. Within time, all names and forms will be destroyed. Everything dissolves into time. Things exist in time, get destroyed by time.
I am that all-devouring time. What you are seeing right now is my form which devours all names and forms. What are you up to right now? Im engaged in destroying the world as you know it. The world as you and I know it is already getting destroyed by Bhagavan. Every second, every millisecond, its constantly getting destroyed.
My reality yesterday is no longer my reality today. My reality today will no longer be my reality tomorrow. So its constant, constantly destroying my world. And I am on the other end, constantly trying to keep my world in a status quo. I want to keep it exactly as I like. I think Im right now in a better situation.
Lets keep it that way. So we have a tug of war between Bhagavan and me. I try to keep it; he wants to destroy it. So when I see his all-destroying power, I ask, why are you doing this? He says, my purpose is clear: I am the time who devours everything.
And right now you are seeing me destroying the world. As you know, and directly addressing. Arjuna said you were afraid that you will kill all these people. You thought that you are so powerful that you will kill all these people. Therefore you were afraid of taking part in this war. He said, I have already killed them all.
From our perspective, we are all alive and trying to survive. But Bhagavan says, theres time. I have already killed all of you -- for whatever time it is, you are going to be killed by time. No matter how many cryogenic clinics open in Richmond -- there is one opened, I guess, recently.
The time may be in years, maybe in millennia. But you will be destroyed by time. Ive already destroyed you as the name and form you exist. I already killed you. Whether you take part in this game or not. You think that you dont want to take part in destroying these people?
These people are already destroyed, because as we learned, what will get destroyed is the conditioning. Only the self is immaculate, permanent, without any limitations. So these people are already destroyed as they exist -- whether they are Karna, Bhishma, or Jayadratha. Even though they seem invincible from your perspective, and they have powers so much greater than yours.
But they are killed by me. So my advice to you, Arjuna, is take charge of your life. Do what you were trained to do. Do what you thought was the purpose of your life. To establish the rule of justice and punish the people who are evil doers. I have already killed them.
You take the credit and then enjoy this kingdom. And thats where Bhagavan stopped. Then Sanjaya now takes a chance to tell Dhritarashtra whats happening. Sanjaya Vacha -- etatshrutva vachanam Kesavasya Krutanjalir vaipamanaha Kiriti namaskritva Bhuya evaha Krishnam Sagadgadam Bhitebhitaha Pranamya. Hes giving a running commentary. He says, having heard these words from Krishna --
That I already killed all of them. I am the one who devours everything. I am the one who kills. You just take the credit and enjoy the victory. Only you can take credit or enjoy victory if you take part in it. If I dont take part, there is no chance.
There is 100% chance of me losing if I dont buy a lottery ticket. Guaranteed 100% chance of not winning the lottery. Thats at least the surest outcome I can say. But if I think I have a chance to win 1 in 10 million, I have to buy a lottery ticket. I have to take part in it. So Bhagavan said, I already decided who the winner is.
You go ahead and buy a lottery ticket if you think you can. But if you dont take part, you will have no chance to win this thing. So Arjuna, therefore get up and do your duty. Result is decided by me. But you have a duty to perform your actions, for which you are trained, which you thought is the purpose of your life. And you must pursue that.
Having heard this, Sanjaya said that this Kiriti, the crowned one, Krutanjali Vepamanha -- his folded palms trembling, because he is still shaken up by this vision of all death and destruction happening constantly in this great self. The self remaining what it is, the names and forms are created in it and getting destroyed all the time. Namaskritva -- having prostrated to him -- Bhuya Eva Aha Krishnam -- he said the following words. He is choked with emotions, choked with the realization of what the self is all about. Up till now, I was in control of my life.
I thought I can control it. I have accomplished things. I have acquired abilities and promises. I suddenly realized that those things are of no value unless there is a support from the Almighty. The consciousness functioning through me. I may be the best architect, but if Im in a coma, it doesnt do any good to anybody.

Arjuna now offers a prayer of deep recognition: Krishna is greater than the Powers of creation, the First Cause, Infinite, the Lord of Lords. He declares Krishna to be the Primal God, the Ancient, the Knower, the Knowledge and the Final Home... the Wind, Death, Fire, Water, the Moon, the Father and the Grandfather. This comprehensive list shows Arjuna seeing Krishna not as one god among many but as the source and essence of all divine principles and natural forces.
The teaching here is about the relationship between the many and the One. We worship different aspects of divinity - some pray to a nurturing mother aspect, others to a powerful protector, still others to wisdom or prosperity. Arjunas vision reveals that all these are expressions of one reality. Wind, Death, Fire, Water - seemingly separate forces - are all manifestations of the same supreme consciousness. This does not diminish the deities but reveals their ultimate unity.
For todays practice, notice the divine in multiple forms throughout your day. See consciousness in the sustaining power of your breath (Vayu), in the natural limits and endings you encounter (Yama), in the transformative fire of your digestion and passion (Agni), in the flowing adaptability of water. Instead of thinking this is different from that, practice seeing each as a face of the same underlying reality. When you say namaste to someone, recognize you are bowing to the same consciousness that looks out through your own eyes. This practice of seeing unity in diversity is the practical application of Arjunas vision.
